author.name: A.R.Pyx
bio: I write historical fiction for readers who want adventure with real weight: hidden histories, moral pressure, and characters forced to act when the world begins to tilt.

I’m drawn to periods of transition — for now I have been exploring the 1890s and the 1930s — when old certainties are breaking apart, and ordinary people must decide what they are willing to protect, betray, or become.

My work grows out of a long fascination with archaeology and the past. Now I have decided to explore adventure fiction to tell stories about it. I’m interested in the line where documented history ends, and imagination begins, but real methods can help shape each other.

Currently, I am exploring what aspects of archaeology can be depicted in an adventure story and how that will come together. I intend to do it using different approaches for the same restless spirit, as if they were lenses:
  • Hic Non Sunt Dracones — a Victorian-era novella in the King Solomon’s Mines tradition.
  • Echoes of Lost Worlds — a 1930s archaeological thriller series indebted to Indiana Jones. 1934: Caught in the Crossroads, its first book, is already out.
  • And more, still ahead: a science-fiction entry, a cozy mystery, and a contemporary story, each chasing what people risk in pursuit of what’s been lost.

1934: Caught in the Crossroads is my debut novel. It stands on its own, but it also opens the door to a wider fictional world rooted in real places, real tensions, and the enduring human habit of chasing meaning through the ruins.
